lesson.title: Exact instructions
lesson.subtitle: Robots do exactly what you say

video.title: Exact instructions: Robots do exactly what you say
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Code is typed out on a card, left to right in both languages. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Amina Bello — the students’ teacher (main character)
Mr Okafor — the students’ science teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice, talking to the student (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.narration: I told my robot: put jam on the bread. It picked up the whole jar and put it on the bread! The robot did exactly what I said.
Today: how to give a robot exact instructions.
A robot is not like a friend. A friend can guess what you mean. A robot can’t guess. It does exactly what you say, step by step.
A list of exact steps in order is called an algorithm. Brushing your teeth has an algorithm. Wet the brush, add toothpaste, brush, then rinse.
The order matters too. If you rinse first and add toothpaste last, it goes wrong. Robots need the right steps, in the right order.
Here is a robot on a grid. It has three cards: forward, turn left and turn right. Turning does not move it. It only changes the way it looks.
Quick check! The robot looks up. The target is on its right, one square away. Which card comes first?
Turn right first. Now the robot faces the target. Then one forward card, and it gets there.
In the app, open Program a robot. Put the cards in order and press Run. Try grids one, two and three.
Your turn. I say only: tidy the desk. Who understands that, a friend or a robot?
A friend. Remember: an algorithm is exact steps, in order. A robot does exactly what you say. And the order of the steps matters.
Try it yourself: program a person. Write exact steps to draw a simple house. Give them to a friend or someone at home, and see what they draw!

checkpoints.prompt: The robot looks up. The target is one square to its right. Which card first?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — first turn right to face the target, then go forward.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — the robot must face the target before it moves. Turn right first.

checkpoints.prompt: “Tidy the desk.” Who understands that, with no more steps?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — a friend can guess. A robot needs every step: pick up the book, put it on the shelf…
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a robot can’t guess what tidy means. It needs every exact step.
